alignment_log.scope: Initial alignment pass: CA CTE (ICT) anchor standards only.
alignment_log.note: The post's own appendix already states the honest scope: this lesson sits outside California's 9-12 CS core on purpose (that framework doesn't cover electrical measurement), and names the two CTE anchors that do fit. This carrier keeps exactly that scope rather than padding it -- no castandards, apcsp, or CSTA entries, since none of those frameworks has anything to check it against. No SEL catalog fits either; this is a procedural/technical-skill lesson with no identity, relationship, or emotional-regulation content.

locator_titles.kilo-and-milli: Kilo & Milli: Borrowing the Meter Stick to Teach Electrical Units

meta.caveat: A single blog post, not a chaptered source -- locator_kind is "none". First post in the porttack.com Hardware category carrier; a physical-computing/electronics lesson that doesn't fit the Coding, SEL, or Society buckets gets its own locator here rather than a new carrier file.

10.7.note: Direct quote match, named in the post's own appendix: the standard's 'kilo, mega, giga, and tera' examples are written with data sizes in mind, but the competency -- fluency with SI prefixes as a scale factor -- is exactly what this lesson teaches, applied to volts/amps/ohms instead.

5.7.note: The chaining exercise (converting across two steps by repeating the same divide/multiply-by-1000 rule) is a small, concrete instance of this standard's iterative problem-solving, as the post's own appendix already names.
